t2m.seo.title: Text to Mind Map — Convert text into structured mind maps
t2m.seo.description: Turn structured text into mind maps with a keyboard-friendly editor, flexible layouts, rich node details and export options.
t2m.hero.subtitle: A fast, keyboard-friendly editor that turns plain text into structured mind maps you can rearrange, style and export.
t2m.hero.stat.0.label: Outline ideas in a structured editor
t2m.hero.stat.1.label: View changes as a visual mind map
t2m.hero.stat.2.label: Save outputs in practical formats
t2m.trust.title: Your data stays in your browser
t2m.trust.body: Text to Mind Map is designed as a local-first tool. Documents live in your browser's storage — they are not uploaded to a server for processing, and there is no account to create.
t2m.trust.points.0.title: No account required
t2m.trust.points.0.body: Open the app and start working immediately. No sign-up, no profile.
t2m.trust.points.1.title: No server uploads
t2m.trust.points.1.body: Text and maps are processed in the browser. Content is not sent to a server for parsing or rendering.
t2m.trust.points.2.title: Local-first storage
t2m.trust.points.2.body: Documents are saved in your browser. You choose when to export or clear them.
t2m.coreValue.title: Why it helps
t2m.coreValue.body: Move from written notes to a visual structure without leaving one workflow. Type an outline with keyboard controls, review the generated map, then adjust the structure when it needs to change.
t2m.showcase.title: See it in action
t2m.showcase.subtitle: Text on the left, a live map on the right — the outline and the map stay in sync as you type.
t2m.showcase.shot1.caption: Type an outline, get a map
t2m.showcase.shot1.body: Tab to indent, Enter for a new sibling, Shift+Tab to outdent. The outline and the map update together as you type.
t2m.features.title: Key features
t2m.features.subtitle: Tools for turning written structure into a clear visual map.
t2m.features.items.0.title: Keyboard-first speed
t2m.features.items.0.body: Use Tab to create a sub-node, or Shift+Tab to move back a level while outlining.
t2m.features.items.1.title: Node details
t2m.features.items.1.body: Attach context to nodes with details that support planning, research and documentation.
t2m.features.items.2.title: Flexible layouts
t2m.features.items.2.body: Switch between supported map and tree layouts to suit the structure of your content.
t2m.features.items.3.title: Fully interactive
t2m.features.items.3.body: Reorganise the map by dragging nodes into the structure that best reflects your work.
t2m.features.items.4.title: Visual customisation
t2m.features.items.4.body: Adjust branch and level colours to make larger maps easier to scan.
t2m.features.items.5.title: Workspaces and undo
t2m.features.items.5.body: Organise work into dedicated spaces and use undo or redo while editing.
t2m.features.items.6.title: Easy export
t2m.features.items.6.body: Export maps to text, JSON or image formats for practical reuse.
t2m.useCases.title: Common use cases
t2m.useCases.subtitle: Useful for turning notes, plans and structured thinking into visual form.
t2m.useCases.groups.0.items.0.title: Lecture and study notes
t2m.useCases.groups.0.items.0.body: Convert notes into a visual structure for review, comparison and revision.
t2m.useCases.groups.0.items.1.title: Essay planning
t2m.useCases.groups.0.items.1.body: Map out arguments, supporting points and source notes in a structured format.
t2m.useCases.groups.1.items.0.title: Project scoping
t2m.useCases.groups.1.items.0.body: Outline requirements, adjust scope and export structured outputs for documentation.
t2m.useCases.groups.1.items.1.title: Knowledge bases
t2m.useCases.groups.1.items.1.body: Organise concepts, references and related decisions as a visual map.
t2m.useCases.groups.2.items.0.title: System and flow diagrams
t2m.useCases.groups.2.items.0.body: Map out code structures, API endpoints or user journeys with clear tree diagrams.
t2m.useCases.groups.2.items.1.title: Content planning
t2m.useCases.groups.2.items.1.body: Organise outlines, pillars and research notes in one visual structure.
t2m.quickStart.title: How to start
t2m.quickStart.subtitle: Five steps from a blank page to a map you can export.
t2m.quickStart.steps.0.title: Start typing
t2m.quickStart.steps.0.body: Open the editor and write your central idea.
t2m.quickStart.steps.1.title: Branch out
t2m.quickStart.steps.1.body: Press Enter for a new line, Tab to create a sub-node, and Shift+Tab to outdent.
t2m.quickStart.steps.2.title: Add context
t2m.quickStart.steps.2.body: Select a node to review or add supporting details.
t2m.quickStart.steps.3.title: Adjust the map
t2m.quickStart.steps.3.body: Drag nodes to change hierarchy, adjust colours and pick a suitable layout.
t2m.quickStart.steps.4.title: Export
t2m.quickStart.steps.4.body: Export as an image, JSON or text file when the map is ready.
t2m.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
t2m.faq.items.0.question: Where is my data stored?
t2m.faq.items.0.answer: Documents are stored in your browser's local storage. They are not uploaded to a server for parsing or rendering.
t2m.faq.items.1.question: Is this tool free to use?
t2m.faq.items.1.answer: The app is free to use. Reasonable limits may apply so the service can stay available for everyone.
t2m.faq.items.2.question: Do I need an account or an internet connection?
t2m.faq.items.2.answer: No account is required. An internet connection is needed to load the app; once open, editing works in the browser.
t2m.faq.items.3.question: How do I move my work between browsers or devices?
t2m.faq.items.3.answer: Use the export options to save a copy, then import that file into another browser when you need to continue.
t2m.closing.title: Ready to map your next idea?
t2m.closing.body: Start with text, shape the structure and export a visual map when it is ready.

guide.seo.title: How to Make a Mind Map from Text — Step-by-Step Guide
guide.seo.description: Learn how to turn plain text or an outline into a structured mind map: indenting, quick commands, layouts, colours, Google Drive sync, and exporting your finished map.
guide.hero.title: How to turn text into a mind map
guide.hero.subtitle: A practical, step-by-step walkthrough of writing an outline and watching it become a visual mind map — no design tools required.
guide.intro: Mind mapping usually starts with a blank canvas and a mouse, which slows down the moment you're trying to think fastest. Text to Mind Map flips that: you write a simple indented outline, and the map builds itself as you type. This guide walks through the whole workflow, from your first line of text to an exported image.
guide.closing.title: Try it with your own notes
guide.closing.body: Open the editor and turn your next outline into a map in a few minutes.
useCases.seo.title: Mind Mapping Use Cases — Study, Planning, Brainstorming & More
useCases.seo.description: See how a text-based mind map tool fits study notes, project planning, brainstorming, content outlines, technical documentation, and multi-device workflows backed up with Google Drive.
useCases.hero.title: What people build with a text-to-mind-map tool
useCases.hero.subtitle: The same outline-to-map workflow adapts to very different kinds of thinking. A few common patterns are below.
useCases.closing.title: Have a use case not listed here?
useCases.closing.body: The core workflow — write an outline, watch it become a map — adapts to most kinds of structured thinking.
shortcuts.seo.title: Keyboard Shortcuts & Quick Commands — Text to Mind Map
shortcuts.seo.description: Full reference of keyboard shortcuts for the text editor and mind map view, the quick command list for setting node text, colour, links and images, and how Google Drive sync works.
shortcuts.hero.title: Keyboard shortcuts & quick commands
shortcuts.hero.subtitle: Every shortcut and quick command used to build and reorganise a map without leaving the keyboard.
shortcuts.quickCommandsSubtitle: Type your configured trigger key at the start of a line to open the quick command menu, then choose one of the following.
shortcuts.closing.title: Keep this page handy
shortcuts.closing.body: Bookmark this reference, or open the app and try the shortcuts directly in the editor.
templates.seo.title: Free Mind Map Templates & Examples — Copy, Paste, Customise
templates.seo.description: Ready-to-use mind map templates for study notes, project planning, SWOT analysis, brainstorming, meeting notes and content outlines. Paste one in and start editing.
templates.hero.title: Mind map templates you can start from
templates.hero.subtitle: Each template is a plain-text outline — copy it, paste it into the editor, and it becomes a fully structured, editable mind map instantly.
templates.intro: A blank page is the hardest part of any mind map. These templates give you a starting structure for common situations, written as plain indented text so they work with the outline editor exactly the way your own notes would. Paste one in, then rename the nodes, add or remove branches, and adjust colours or layout to fit your project.
templates.pasteHint: then paste it into the editor
templates.closing.title: Start from a template, make it your own
templates.closing.body: Copy an outline above, paste it into the editor, and reshape it into your own map in a couple of minutes.
